# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (15,512 packets, 2026-02-28 23:55:06 to 2026-03-01 04:16:35, ~4h21m). No IDS/alert files were provided alongside the capture, only the pcap.

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 | Source of all malicious traffic; DHCP request/ack |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad | ARP replies for 10.2.28.88; matches DHCP client MAC |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR | DHCP Option 12 (hostname) in DHCP Request/ACK; confirmed by NBNS name registration (`DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR<00>`, `<20>`) |
| Logged-in user | brolf | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 10.2.28.88 and DC 10.2.28.2, the only user principal observed from this host |
| AD domain | easyas123.tech (NetBIOS EASYAS123) | DNS queries to `EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech`, `_ldap._tcp...easyas123.tech`; NBNS `EASYAS123<1d>/<1e>` |
| LAN | 10.2.28.0/24, gateway/DC 10.2.28.1 (DHCP server) / 10.2.28.2 (domain controller) | DHCP, LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos/SMB2/DCE-RPC volume to 10.2.28.2 |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT (NetSupport Manager abused as a remote access trojan).**

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The HTTP client explicitly self-identifies with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every beacon, and the C2 traffic uses the well-documented NetSupport RAT check-in pattern:
- Fixed URI `POST /fakeurl.htm`
- Plaintext HTTP body `CMD=POLL\r\nINFO=1\r\nACK=1\r\n` (client) with `200 OK` responses from the server (this is the standard NetSupport client remote-control (NSM) protocol poll/ack handshake, not a custom C2 protocol)
- Beacon interval of ~60 seconds, sustained for the entire 15,682-second capture (264 POSTs total, first at t=45s, last at t=15682s)

No malware binary/dropper was transferred in this capture window (checked via `--export-objects http`; only benign Windows Update, Adobe MAU, OCSP, and Edge telemetry objects were exported). This means the capture shows an **already-installed, actively beaconing** NetSupport RAT client, not the initial infection/delivery. The delivery vector is not observable in this pcap.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `45.131.214.85:443` — destination of all 264 `POST /fakeurl.htm` beacons from 10.2.28.88. Despite port 443, the traffic is plaintext HTTP, not TLS (confirmed via `http.request`/`http.response` dissection on that port, no TLS ClientHello to this IP).

**Malicious domain**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolved to 45.131.214.85 at 2026-02-28 23:55:51 (DNS A-record answer), immediately preceding the first C2 POST.

**Malicious URL**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — NetSupport RAT poll/check-in endpoint, requested 264 times with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`.

**File names / hashes**
- None. No executable or dropper transfer is present in this capture; the RAT client is already resident and only its check-in traffic was captured. No file to hash.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)

- `10.2.28.2` — internal domain controller (LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos/SMB2/DCE-RPC), expected AD traffic.
- Microsoft/Windows telemetry, Windows Update (`ctldl.windowsupdate.com`), BITS downloads (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), OCSP (`ocsp.digicert.com`), Adobe ARM (`acroipm2.adobe.com`), Edge/Bing/MSN, NVIDIA GFE — normal enterprise workstation background noise.
- `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (resolves to Akamai 23.64.147.24) — one TLS-encrypted connection at t=44.5s, seconds before the first C2 beacon. Content is encrypted and unobservable, so this cannot be confirmed as a delivery/gate site; flagged as timing-adjacent but not asserted as an IOC.
- Google Cast, WPAD, LLMNR/SSDP/mDNS discovery chatter — standard Windows LAN noise.

## Summary

Windows workstation DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as domain user `brolf` on the `easyas123.tech` AD network, is running an active NetSupport RAT implant identified by its literal `NetSupport Manager/1.3` user-agent and its `POST /fakeurl.htm` poll/ack protocol. The implant has been beaconing every ~60 seconds for the full 4-hour-21-minute capture to `vadusa.xyz` (45.131.214.85:443) over plaintext HTTP. The infection was already established before this capture began; no delivery mechanism or dropped payload is visible in the traffic captured here.
